Cuevas Pintadas de Guachipas is an archaeological site in the Las Juntas area of Salta Province. Natural shelters in the red sandstone cliffs preserve paintings made by the ancient inhabitants of northwestern Argentina. Particularly distinctive are the “shield people”: human figures with broad, patterned bodies. Images of camelids, birds, and other animals appear alongside them.

The paintings offer a glimpse of how the people of these valleys depicted their world through color and symbols. The landscape is part of the experience, too: warm-colored stone, rocky outcrops, and overhangs frame the ancient compositions. The site is protected as part of Argentina’s historical heritage; visitors should keep their distance from the paintings and follow the visiting rules.

Cuiabá is the starting and finishing point for itineraries across the Northern Pantanal. From here, travelers head through Poconé toward the Transpantaneira road and nature lodges.

Itineraries also connect the city with trips to the clear waters of Bom Jardim and the waterfalls of Chapada dos Guimarães. After exploring these natural areas, travelers return to Cuiabá for an overnight stay or an onward flight.

At Cultuurtuin, simply slowing down can turn a walk into a birdwatching experience. Sunlight filters through the crowns of large trees in patches, while calls echo among the branches. The guide stops and points out movement in the leaves, and what appeared to be an ordinary green canopy suddenly teems with life. This walk is a rewarding addition to a visit to Paramaribo.

The botanical garden forms part of the Cultuurtuin complex and preserves areas of mature woodland. Native and introduced tropical trees grow here. The forest paths and birds are particularly appealing to visitors: manakins, flycatchers, and woodpeckers invite you to pause along short stretches of the trail and notice details that are easy to miss.

On Ada Tours’ birdwatching itinerary, Cultuurtuin is visited after a trip to Nieuw Amsterdam. As evening approaches, the search begins for forest owls, including the spectacled owl. These are wild birds, and sightings depend on their activity, the light, and the weather. The guide helps choose the right time and spot birds among the dense vegetation.
